analysis:
All rollouts (baseline and PP) uniformly timed out with zero trace content available. This is a systematic failure with no execution variance — the agent never produced an answer in any attempt. Without any trace data (no searches, no reasoning, no playbook citations, no XML tags), root-cause diagnosis must be inferred from the failure pattern itself.

The most significant observation is that the existing playbook's budget-control mechanism is SEARCH-COUNT-BASED ([1f931f4e]: Hard Budget Stop at 40 Searches) but the failure is TIME-BASED. These are fundamentally different constraints. The agent could be: (a) spending excessive time per search cycle reasoning about which of 14+ playbook entries to consult, (b) generating very long reasoning chains between searches, (c) stuck in early-stage planning/decomposition before even beginning to search, or (d) encountering a task that requires many searches and the per-search overhead exceeds the wall-clock budget.

Key structural concern: the playbook has grown to 14 entries, many of which are multi-step procedures with nested checklists. Before each search, the agent may be cross-referencing multiple entries, running trigger checks, and performing constraint scoring — all of which consume time without generating searchable progress. The playbook has NO guidance on time management, early action, or keeping per-search overhead low.

A second concern is the absence of an EARLY COMMIT signal. Entry [1f931f4e] triggers at search 40, but if the agent never reaches 40 searches due to time-per-search overhead, the rule never fires. There is no entry that says 'if you have been working for N minutes and have fewer than X searches completed, something is wrong — simplify and accelerate.'

A third concern is the lack of a FAST-START directive. Many entries (decomposition, distinctiveness triage, clue listing) encourage extensive pre-search reasoning. For difficult tasks, this front-loaded planning phase could consume a disproportionate share of the time budget before any search is issued.

Since no trace content exists, I cannot attribute credit or blame to any specific entry with confidence. All entries are tagged neutral. The timeout is the only signal, and it points to a COVERAGE GAP: the playbook lacks wall-clock time awareness.
